newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zeroual's allies give pitch for June 5 poll.
newsitem.headline: Zeroual's allies give pitch for June 5 poll.

text.p: The newly created Algerian National Democratic Rally (RND), a party grouping President Liamine Zeroual's core political supporters, said on Saturday it would contest every seat in the June 5 parliamentary polls.

"The RND aspires to score well in order to be well-represented in the future legislative body and the party is fully convinced of the policy it has set out," said the group's leader, Abdelkader Bensalah..

Bensalah, quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS as speaking at a news conference in Algiers, said the National Democratic Rally was born to "restore hope to the Algerians and to fill a political vacuum".
Bensalah, who is the president of the government-appointed Transitional National Council, criticised the widespread belief that his group is the "party of the current power".
"Our movement is a party like the others. It was set up out of conviction, according to the party law, to bring about political change and help pulling the country out of the crisis."

Algeria has been without a parliament since January 1992 when army-backed authorities cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead. About 60,000 people have died in the five years of violence between government forces and Moslem guerrillas.
The RND is one of about 60 parties that will compete for seats in the parliamentary elections.
Opposition party leaders fear the RND may get a majority in the polls thanks to its ties with the current government.
"The president had several times repeated that he is the president of all Algerians and his party is all Algeria," said Bensalah.
Algerians will be voting for a 380-seat National Assembly, which with a 144-seat National Council will form the country's parliament.
Two thirds of the National Council will be designated by elected local authorities while the other third will be picked by the president.
